summary: Monday deep-dive team meeting run by Chris Klevan — the weekly numbers review rather than the lighter daily format. Wins, then a call-by-call post-mortem of the previous week for each closer, then projections are re-cut and moved into later weeks, then announcements on ads and marketing, and finally a group review of Andrew Musial's closed call with Dan Keogh. Chris teaches the team the reporting format he wants going forward: slots booked, calls shown, calls closed, deposits taken, most common objection, and the one thing to focus on next week. The recording cuts off mid-review.
notable: Chris counted two unpaid deposits as closed units to arrive at Richard's close rate — 'so that's technically three units, right?... so then you close three out of nine, so that's 33%' — over Richard's objection that 'they're not in yet.'

Andrew took a deposit from a prospect who, unaware the phone line was still open after the Zoom ended, told his wife he had only paid to get rid of the rep: 'oh yeah, I had to pay this guy, but I don't think he will. Yeah, just to get rid of me, I think.' Chris: 'Yeah, sometimes people will do that.'

Andrew is still holding a $100 deposit from a prospect who got scared; Chris told him to refund it specifically to avoid a chargeback — 'if they get super scared and they don't want to get on the phone with you again, then they might just charge it back.'

Andrew's closed deal was structured on credit for a prospect with no liquid cash who had just paid $300,000 cash for a house and taken a second job: 'he could do six times 1,200... he told me his credit score was 700-something, and I was like, dude, put it on a credit card.'

Financing is a live and expanding channel — PayVide/Paiva, PayPal Credit, and 'we're working on a couple different financing partners.' Several prospects were declined, including one with a $2,000 credit limit approved for $1,000, and one described as a student.

A publicly visible $200/month Primal University price is anchoring inbound calls for the $6,000 offer. Richard: 'I had someone today, and he read that online... he said like, yeah, I wouldn't have booked a meeting if it was six grand.' Chris confirmed it is a known problem and deliberately deprioritised behind marketing work.
Chris's reporting standard, stated for the team: slots booked, calls shown, calls closed, deposits taken, most common objection, and the single focus for the next week.

Richard's week: nine live calls, one unit at 6K, two deposits, two FDQs. His debrief of the Robert Karssiens call in this batch: 'he expected $3,000, and he said, like, if it was $3,000, I would have done it, but I'm not doing $6,000 like this.' Chris pressed on whether he went for a deposit; Richard said no.

Andrew continued to identify prospects by sexual orientation and ethnicity — 'Because I pressured the gay guy', 'Tom, the gay one', 'Eddie, the Asian guy' — three days after Chris corrected exactly this in the 07/03 meeting. No correction this time.

Andrew's earlier read that a prospect hung up on him was wrong — 'he actually didn't hang up. He texted me that his phone got, he was dead' — after both he and Chris had speculated the prospect was acting.

Ads are currently retargeting warm traffic only, no cold traffic. Instagram output is going from one post a day to 30 pieces a week, messaging is being repositioned toward coaching, and a new VSL is about to be shot.
Recurring payments do not count toward projections — 'This is just new cash.'
